It is argued by Ld. counsel for the accused that the accused is innocent.
The Prosecution has only examined the complainant/ Ravi Khanna in support of the charge for the offence of attempt to murder of the complainant by accused Rakesh Babul.
The complainant's testimony is full of flip-flops and it is replete with contradictions and inconsistencies.
It is submitted that a free fight occurred between the inmates of Ward No. 8 of Jail No. 4, Tihar Jail where number of inmates were involved.
Both the complainant as well as accused received stab injuries in the said scuffle.

The Prosecution has not been able to establish beyond reasonable doubt that the complainant was attacked by accused and even the statement of complainant is not consistent as to who has attacked the complainant and was involved in stabbing of the complainant.

Further, the number of inmates and Warders were present at the time of incident, however, no efforts were made to record the statement of independent witness to corroborate the statement of the complainant.
It is also urged that as per the MLC of the accused on record Ex.PW6/A (colly), even he received stab injuries.
No fair investigation was carried out by IO to book the inmates involved in assaulting the accused.
On these grounds, it is stated that the Prosecution has not been able to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt and accused is entitled to acquittal.

The key witness of the Prosecution in this case is PW-1/complainant Ravi Khanna.

It is no longer res-inegra that the testimony of a sole witness is sufficient to return the finding of guilt against the accused, provided such testimony is completely cogent, credible, consistent, coherent and truthful.
Only when the testimony of sole witness is completely impeccable and unshaken, it can form the basis of conviction of the accused.
The testimony of complainant/PW1 has to be tested on the touchstone of this principle of law.
The testimony of complainant/PW-1 has not remained consistent and he has made improvements in his statement recorded from time to time.

In his first statement recorded in the hospital based on which the SC No. 780/2022 " State v. Rakesh Babul"
present FIR has been registered against the accused, the complainant has named two accused persons Rakesh @ Babul and Ashu.
He stated that Ashu caught hold of him from behind and then accused Rakesh @ Babul attacked him with a knife like object near his armpit and stabbed him there three-four times.
Both Ashu and Rakesh have beaten him mercilessly before he was attacked with a knife like object by accused Rakesh @ Babul.

However, in the supplementary statement recorded u/s. 161 Cr.P.C.,
he has given clean chit to Ashu and stated that only Rakesh attacked and stabbed him with a knife like object and Ashu saved him from the assault of accused Rakesh.
In his testimony recorded in the Court, PW-1 against changed his statement and stated that at the time of incident, he was standing outside his Barrack with Aman and Satbir.
To take revenge of earlier altercation, the Inmate Ravi @ Pappi came along with Ashu and Rakesh.
He further stated that Aman went from there and accused Rakesh inflicted injuries on him with a sharp spoon.
Then he added that he was attacked by Aman and Aman had inflicted serious injuries under his armpit and on his back.
He was saved from Aman by other inmates.

So, the testimony of PW-1/complainant loses its credibility and truthfulness because SC No.

The testimony of PW-11 SI Kunal Sandhu in isolation is not sufficient to establish the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt.
The IO/PW-11 is not the eye witness and has joined the investigation only on 18.06.2022.

PW-11 in his evidence identified the accused and the injured in the CCTV footage dated 23.03.2022 from 16:00:50 hours to 16:02:00 hours pertaining to Ward No.
8 of Jail No. 4 of park view camera, and also stated that the accused is seen inflicting injuries on the State vs Rakesh @ Babul on 30 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120119122/
9 complainant in the said CCTV footage.
Once the complainant himself has disowned the said CCTV footages and stated affirmatively that it does not capture the incident, the aforesaid statement/evidence of IO loses its significance.
Even otherwise, the camera in question has captured the video from a considerable distance.
So, neither the faces of inmates nor incident is clearly visible in the said CCTV footages.
In these circumstances, the CCTV footages does not prove the incident or involvement of the accused.
18. Apart from that the MLC of accused, Ex.PW6/A (colly.), shows that he has also received stab injuries in the incident.

In State of M.P. v. Mishrilal, (2003) 9 SCC 426, Hon'ble Apex Court held as under:
"17. Non-explanation of the injuries sustained by the accused: The last and which appears to be fatal to the prosecution case is SC No. 780/2022 " State v. Rakesh Babul"

sentences.text: As already said, accused Mishrilal received as many as five injuries, which were dangerous to life.
Madhusudan and Jamuna prasad received simple injuries.
In Ext. P-1 as well as in the entire deposition of PWs, the prosecution has not explained the injuries sustained by the accused.
In the background of the defence, as set up by the accused, it was incumbent on the part of the prosecution, to have explained the injuries sustained by the accused.

The defence version is that on the bullock cart of Babulal having retreated, the complainant party -- Maharaj Singh, Gopal, Mathura Lal, Lakhan, Jagdish, Mulia, Kailash and Karan Singh came with lathis and farsa.

Mathura Lal hit Mishrilal's head with the farsa and Babulal,
Maharaj Singh and Karan Singh beat Mishrilal with lathis.
Madhusudan ran to save his father Mishrilal and they also beat him.
When Jamunaprasad came to save, he was also beaten up and on that Jamunaprasad ran towards the house and made two fires in the air to save his father.
It is the case of the defence that the bullet, which struck Bhavarsingh, came from the house of Babulal.

In the face of the defence version, which competes in probability with that of the prosecution case, it was mandatory on the part of the prosecution to have explained the injuries sustained by the accused and non-explanation of the injuries is fatal to the prosecution case.

In Lakshmi Singh v. State of Bihar [(1976) 4 SCC 394 : 1976 SCC (Cri) 671] referring to earlier decisions in Mohar Rai v. State of Bihar [AIR 1968 SC 1281 : (1968) 3 SCR 525 : 1968 Cri LJ 1479] it was held by this Court: (SCC pp.
401-02, para 12) SC No. 780/2022 " State v. Rakesh Babul"

sentences.text:
where the prosecution fails to explain the injuries on the accused, two results follow:
(1) that the evidence of the prosecution witnesses is untrue; and (2) that the injuries probabilise the plea taken by the appellants.

... in a murder case, the non-explanation of the injuries sustained by the accused at about the time of the occurrence or in the course of altercation is a very important circumstance from which the court can draw the following inferences:
State vs Rakesh @ Babul on 30 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120119122/
10 (1) that the prosecution has suppressed the genesis and the origin of the occurrence and has thus not presented the true version; (2) that the witnesses who have denied the presence of the injuries on the person of the accused are lying on a most material point and therefore their evidence is unreliable; (3) that in case there is a defence version which explains the injuries on the person of the accused it is rendered probable so as to throw doubt on the prosecution case.

The omission on the part of the prosecution to explain the injuries on the person of the accused assumes much greater importance where the evidence consists of interested or inimical witnesses or where the defence gives a version which competes in probability with that of the prosecution one. ...
(However) there may be cases where the non-explanation of the injuries by the prosecution may not affect the prosecution case.

This principle would obviously apply to cases where the injuries sustained by the accused are minor and superficial or where the evidence is so clear and cogent, so independent and disinterested, so probable, consistent and creditworthy, that it far outweighs the effect of the omission on the part of the prosecution to explain the injuries."
SC No. 780/2022 " State v. Rakesh Babul"
The IO/PW-11 has admitted in his cross-examination that in the CCTV footages, four inmates are seen assaulting the accused.
However, no efforts were admittedly made by the Investigating Agency to establish the identity of the inmates who are assaulting the accused in CCTV footages.

The punishment Ticket Ex-PW4/B issued to the complainant/ Ravi and accused Rakesh records that "During the enquiry, it was revealed that while the warder was manning the gate, he heard loud shouts of inmates from the ground.
Then the warder immediately rushed towards the spot and saw both the above-mentioned inmates were attacking each other with sharp object.
The blood was oozing out profusely of both the inmates". PW-11 also stated in cross- examination that no cross FIR was registered regarding the assault upon the accused.
Thus, even the fair and impartial investigation has not been conducted in the present matter by the IO.
So, it is not clear whether the accused was the victim or the assailant.
This further dents the case of prosecution and version of incident as deposed by the complainant remains under shadow of doubt.
19. The Prosecution is bound to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.
There is a long distance between the proposition that the case against the accused "must be true" and "may be true".
The said long distance has to be bridged by the Prosecution.
In the present matter, the evidence of sole witness/complainant is not credible, truthful and worthy of reliance.

There is no other credible evidence i.e. documentary or SC No. 780/2022 " State v. Rakesh Babul"
oral or digital to establish the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt.
20. In the light of above discussions, it is concluded that the Prosecution has failed to prove the case against the accused for the charge of offence punishable u/s. 307 IPC beyond reasonable doubt.
Accordingly, accused is acquitted of the charge for the offence punishable u/s. 307 IPC.

opennyai_summary.arguments:
Both the complainant as well as accused received stab injuries in the said scuffle.
The Prosecution has not been able to establish beyond reasonable doubt that the complainant was attacked by accused and even the statement of complainant is not consistent as to who has attacked the complainant and was involved in stabbing of the complainant.
Further, the number of inmates and Warders were present at the time of incident, however, no efforts were made to record the statement of independent witness to corroborate the statement of the complainant.
No fair investigation was carried out by IO to book the inmates involved in assaulting the accused.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is no longer res-inegra that the testimony of a sole witness is sufficient to return the finding of guilt against the accused, provided such testimony is completely cogent, credible, consistent, coherent and truthful.
Only when the testimony of sole witness is completely impeccable and unshaken, it can form the basis of conviction of the accused.
The testimony of complainant/PW1 has to be tested on the touchstone of this principle of law.
The testimony of complainant/PW-1 has not remained consistent and he has made improvements in his statement recorded from time to time.
So, no independent corroborative evidence has been produced by the Prosecution to establish the guilt of the accused and only the statement of the complainant has been relied on by the Prosecution which does not inspire confidence of court.
It is correct that in the CCTV footage, four inmates are seen assaulting accused.
No cross FIR was registered regarding the assault upon accused.
It is correct that during investigation, the names of the inmates who were assaulting were not revealed except one of the inmate namely Aman.
During investigation, I had not served any notice to Jail Supdt for establishing the identity of the remaining inmates who are seen assaulting accused in the CCTV footage.
It is correct that as per the CCTV footage, after initial assault by accused, four or five inmates are seen assaulting accused.
No FIR was registered against the said inmates who are seen assaulting accused.
As per MLC, the nature of injuries are opined to be 'simple' and the said injury cannot be termed to injury dangerous to life.
The testimony of PW-11 SI Kunal Sandhu in isolation is not sufficient to establish the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt.
So, neither the faces of inmates nor incident is clearly visible in the said CCTV footages.
In these circumstances, the CCTV footages does not prove the incident or involvement of the accused.
18. Apart from that the MLC of accused, Ex.PW6/A (colly.), shows that he has also received stab injuries in the incident.
